findings.message: This only fixes one case of the credential leak (B1). `RepoUrl` rejects a URL that contains a user or token, but `packages/mcp/src/server.ts:41` writes the raw `args` to the append-only `core.trace_event` before `registry.call` validates them. The refusal therefore comes after the token is already stored for good. The refine also catches only the `scheme://user@` form. A token in scp form (`x-access-token:ghp_x@github.com:org/repo`) passes the refine, and `normaliseRepo` then strips it, so the call succeeds and the token stays in the trace. The new test checks only the service's error message. It never calls the tool over MCP and never looks at the trace row. Fix: redact the userinfo in URL-shaped args (or in all string args) inside `traceStep`/the MCP handler before the trace write. Also refuse any `user:secret@` prefix in every form. Add a tool-level test that calls the tool and then asserts the trace row holds no token.
findings.scenario: A PM in chat runs `link_project_repo` with repoUrl `https://x-access-token:ghp_abc@github.com/o/r` → the tool returns 'remove the user name or token', but `core.trace_event` already holds `ghp_abc` permanently. An MCP client sends `sync_specclaw` with repoUrl `bot:ghp_abc@github.com:o/r` → the push is accepted and the token is in the trace.

findings.message: The 'default branch covers everything' gate trusts a `defaultRef` that the client sends, and the schema falls back to "main" when it is missing. Any MCP caller, or a hand-edited payload, can set `defaultRef` equal to its own lagging branch. That branch then counts as default and overwrites every change with its older title, tasks and meta, which is the regression last round's finding described. Fix: keep the default branch on the project (set when the repo is linked, or read once from the forge) and compare `ref` against that stored value. Don't let the payload decide which ref is trusted. Add a test where a branch push claims `defaultRef` = its own ref.
findings.scenario: A branch `specclaw/102-import`, cut from an old main, pushes with `defaultRef: "specclaw/102-import"` and a newer commit time → `onDefault` is true, and FLT-101's title and tasks fall back to the old branch copy.

findings.message: Records dropped by the branch filter (`p.records.filter(x => onDefault || x.dir === own)`) leave no trace. They are not counted, not listed in `skipped`, and don't set `needsReview`. With the plugin's `defaultRefOf` falling back to "main" whenever `origin/HEAD` isn't set (plugins/amax/scripts/src/read-specclaw.ts:25), this hits real cases: a repo whose default is `master`, a detached-HEAD CI checkout (`ref` = "HEAD"), or a clone with no origin/HEAD. Every record is filtered, and the push returns `outcome: "unchanged"` with zero counts and `needsReview: false`, so `--apply` treats it as fine and nothing ever syncs. The same failure makes the plugin's fallback a fail-open default (B6). Fix: report each filtered record as a skip (e.g. `FLT-101: not this branch's change`). When the ref matches no record at all, return a distinct outcome or set `needsReview`. Have the plugin fail, or send an explicit unknown, instead of guessing "main".
findings.scenario: A repo with default branch `master` and no `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` pushes from master → the plugin sends `defaultRef: "main"`, `ref: "master"`, so every record is filtered → the result is `{outcome:"unchanged", created:0, updated:0, skipped:[], needsReview:false}` and no proposal is ever updated.

findings.message: The new `attempt(ctx, plan, quiet)` path commits writes to `delivery.proposal` (the `synced_commit_at` UPDATE in applyPush) inside a bare `getRuntime().db.transaction`, outside `defineService()`. That write gets no audit row, no service permission check and no events. AGENTS.md core rule 5 says writes go through `defineService()`, and the architecture lists the only three exemptions, which don't include this one. Before this round the bare transaction was always rolled back, so it never mattered. Fix: advance the marks inside a defineService (for example a `delivery.sync.mark` service, audited by count), or always go through `applied` and record the quiet case there.
findings.scenario: Re-push the same state from a newer commit with dryRun=false. The result is outcome 'unchanged', FLT-101/102.synced_commit_at moves to 10:00, and core.audit_event gets no row for that change. The test at sync-push.test.ts:93-94 asserts exactly this: the audit count is unchanged while the mark moved.

findings.message: The lock test stays green with applyPush's early `for update` removed. Without that lock, the first `attempt` still blocks: the other session holds the FLT-102 row lock (from its UPDATE), and `upsertSpecProposal` also locks the project. So `waited` is still true. After the release, that first attempt counts `updated: 1` and is rolled back (keep=false). `applied()` then runs in a fresh transaction, reads the committed 15:00 mark and skips the record as stale. Both assertions pass. The test also plants the competing state with hand-written SQL instead of a second real push. Fix: have the other session hold only the project row lock (no write to FLT-102), and assert that the push is still blocked before upsertSpecProposal runs. Or run two real `pushSpecclaw` calls with a barrier, and check that the result changes when the early lock is removed.
findings.scenario: Delete `for update` from applyPush (push.ts:71) → the test still passes.

findings.message: `STANDING` treats every 'would move back' and 'stale' skip as expected, even when it comes from the default branch. The README and SKILL justify those skips with 'a branch behind main', which doesn't apply to a main push. A main push that would step a phase back points to a real problem, such as a reverted or rewritten state.json. Today it is silent: outcome 'unchanged', no sync_push row, needsReview false, and --apply goes ahead unattended. The classification also works by regex-matching the message strings built in `refusal()`, a second copy of those strings (B4), so rewording a message flips needsReview. Fix: return structured skip reasons ({key, code}) from refusal(), and count move-back and stale as standing only when `!onDefault`.
findings.scenario: Push from main where FLT-101's state.json says 'planned' while amax holds 'building'. Result: { outcome: 'unchanged', skipped: ['FLT-101: would move back from building to planned'], needsReview: false }. No sync_push row is written and the skill's --apply run passes.

findings.message: The erasure test covers two variants (actor only, for_user only) and leaves out the third that the finding named: one person as both actor and for_user on the same row. In the actor case, `for_user_id` is already null, so `expect(after.for_user_id).toBeNull()` checks nothing there. The test also sets `owner_name = null` on every proposal through the owner connection, which changes shared fixture state for later tests.

The generated bundle grew by about 19,700 lines because `repo-url.ts` imports zod, so all of zod and its locales ship with the plugin, while the plugin only uses `normaliseRepo`. Move `normaliseRepo` into a file without zod, and keep the `RepoUrl` schema separate, so the plugin bundle stays small.

Instance fix of the stale-mark finding. Only sync_specclaw advances `proposal.synced_commit_at`. The other writers of the same specclaw rows, the self-sync (`syncSpecclaw` / bin.ts via syncProposal's service) and the `sync_proposal` tool, never set it. The stale gate still has no single source of truth: after a self-sync from a newer main commit, the column still holds the older push time, so an older commit passes the gate and overwrites what the self-sync wrote. Fix: have upsertSpecProposal set `synced_commit_at = greatest(...)` for every writer that knows its commit time, or refuse pushes for rows whose last writer recorded no mark. Add a test that self-syncs and then pushes an older commit.
findings.scenario: Push FLT-102 from specclaw/102-import at 10:00 (mark=10:00). Self-sync imports main at a 15:00 commit, which sets title and tasks from main, and the mark stays 10:00. A branch push at a 12:00 commit is not refused as stale and overwrites main's 15:00 title and tasks.
